programme: STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9 assemble as ISGF3, the canonical transcription factor complex that transduces type I interferon signalling onto interferon-stimulated genes (STAT1 targets include IRF1, SOCS1/3, TAP1, CIITA, ICAM1; STAT2 targets include IRF9, IRF1, OAS1, IFIT2/3, EIF2AK2; IRF9 targets include IFIT1, IFIT3, OAS1, CXCL10, IRF7, STAT1 itself). NFKB1 runs in parallel as the co-activated pro-inflammatory arm that innate-immune sensing normally couples to the same ISGF3 response (its targets TNF, IL6, ICAM1, CCL5, CXCL8, VCAM1 are the classic NF-κB inflammatory output that accompanies an interferon signature).
role_in_a: In papillary kidney carcinoma, an ISGF3/NF-κB signature would be expected to operate through tumour antigen presentation and an inflamed immune microenvironment (STAT1's CIITA and TAP1 targets point at MHC-driven antigen presentation), but the record gives this almost no direct support: IRF9 and STAT2 have no Open Targets association at all, STAT1 sits at the median (0.4869 of 2369 genes) rather than elevated, and NFKB1 is below median (0.1247) for this disease.
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis this is a textbook axis: IFN-β is a first-line disease-modifying therapy, and ISGF3 (STAT1-STAT2-IRF9) is the complex through which it acts, directly supported here by PMID 42267917 documenting enhanced and prolonged IFN responses under long-term IFN-β therapy. NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation is likewise an established contributor to MS/EAE pathology, echoed here by three MS-specific NFKB1 papers (40327306, 41420758, 39855613) on susceptibility genes, a neuroprotective intervention in an EAE model, and a diagnostic gene signature.
shared_axis: Both diseases can independently recruit a type I interferon/NF-κB inflammatory programme — MS through IFN-β-driven demyelinating autoimmunity, and renal papillary carcinoma through the interferon/NF-κB-associated tumour-immune microenvironment that is generically described in kidney cancers — but nothing in this record documents the two diseases sharing this axis as a stated fact; the case rests on each disease separately recruiting the same general innate-immune transcriptional module.
reasoning: The module itself is textbook and nameable purely from the factors (ISGF3 plus its NF-κB partner), and two of its four carrying factors (STAT1, NFKB1) are independently placed in multiple sclerosis by retrieved papers, so this is not a bare co-occurrence. But IRF9 and STAT2 have no disease-specific literature support in either condition, and every Open Targets signal for the kidney side is at or below median with two factors entirely unscored, so the KIRP side of the story is carried by reasoning about renal-tumour immunology in general rather than by anything retrieved for this disease.
support: PMID 42267917 — STAT1/ISGF3 signalling activity in multiple sclerosis via long-term IFN-β therapy; PMID 40327306 — NFKB1 linked to an MS-associated comorbidity (susceptibility genes for MS-induced neuropathic bladder); PMID 41420758 — NFKB1-related neuroprotective compound tested in an EAE (MS model) demyelination paradigm; PMID 39855613 — NFKB1-associated lipid metabolism gene signature used as an MS diagnostic model. No PMID in the material addresses IRF9, STAT2, or any factor in papillary renal cell carcinoma directly.
how_to_falsify: In matched papillary RCC and MS-lesion (or PBMC) samples, ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9 co-occupancy at ISGF3 target promoters (e.g. OAS1, IFIT1/3, CXCL10) alongside NFKB1 occupancy at its inflammatory targets (TNF, IL6, ICAM1); if the two factor sets do not co-bind or co-vary with disease activity in the KIRP tumours the way they do in MS lesions, or if IFN-β/IFN-γ stimulation of KIRP tumour cells fails to induce the same ISGF3 + NF-κB joint signature seen in MS-relevant immune cells, the shared-axis account is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing (brain vs kidney) is anatomically distant, and the shared-axis claim leans on innate-immune signalling being tissue-agnostic rather than on any documented cross-disease fact. The 364 comparisons derive from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts reflect within-cohort replication more than independent confirmation. None of the single-view factors (FOXJ3, FOXO4, ELK4, SMAD2, BCL3, HOXD1, FOSB, KAT7, GTF2IRD1, NPAS1, RFX5, SETBP1) were used, and the tissue-generic exclusion list (ZEB1/ZEB2, TCF4, REST, MEF2C, etc.) does not include STAT1/STAT2/IRF9/NFKB1, so their presence is not simply default brain/kidney signal. The absence of retrieved evidence for IRF9/STAT2/NFKB1 in papillary RCC is a gap in the record, not evidence the connection is novel.
